submissionAttempts.body:
The integration should expect a thrown/rejected `InvalidCursorError` (subclass of `OrdariumError`) with the stable string code **`INVALID_CURSOR`** — not the historic numeric code 27.

What it is: the "observation cursor" is Ordarium's state-change-feed resume position. `OrdariumStateStore.changes(filter, cursor)` delegates to the ledger's `StateChangeFeed.changes()` (ORD-BOOT-0), and `StateChangePage.cursor` is the opaque, durable, filter-independent position a consumer stores and later replays. When that stored cursor is rejected, both ledger implementations throw `InvalidCursorError`:
- decode rejection — cursor is not base64url(JSON `{"c":"<digits>"}`), or the position is not a safe integer ≥ 0 (`decodeStateChangeCursor` in core `ledger.js` and ledger-sqlite `index.js`);
- semantic rejection — the decoded position exceeds the ledger's global change high-water mark (foreign / restored / replaced ledger), checked in `MemoryLedger.changes` and `SqliteLedger.changes`.

Behavioural intent: fail closed, refusing to guess a resume point rather than silently restarting from the beginning of the feed. It is deliberately distinct from `LedgerCorruptError`/`LEDGER_CORRUPT` (damaged ledger content) and from `LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` (ledger lacks the `stateChangeFeed` capability). It is also not in the transient/retry-safe classifications in `src/effects/errors.ts` (`isLedgerBusyError`, `isTransientOperationError`), so it must not be terminalized as an outcome verdict nor retried as contention; the correct handling is fail-closed and re-baseline (discard/re-derive the stored position and take a fresh observation).

Why not 27: `docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md` states numeric code 27 is historic and explicitly "informational, not normative". The pinned dependency is `@ordarium/core@1.3.1` (package.json), whose stable error family in `dist/src/errors.js` uses string codes and defines `INVALID_CURSOR` as the cursor-rejection code; no numeric 27 exists in the pinned artifacts. The two sources are temporally non-co-applicable, and the note's own non-normative status resolves the apparent conflict locally, so the binding answer for this workspace is `InvalidCursorError` / `INVALID_CURSOR`.

Evidence: node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.js (InvalidCursorError → "INVALID_CURSOR"), node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.d.ts (fail-closed, distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT), node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/state.d.ts and types.d.ts (changes()/StateChangeFeed/StateChangePage.cursor), node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/ledger.js and node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js (throw sites), package.json (@ordarium/core 1.3.1), docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md (non-normative historic 27).
